title: Alex Neilan - Sustainable Change Sales Spin
author: Alex Neilan (@alexneilan)

rules.qualification_bmi: 27 BMI+ or at least 9 kgs (1.5 stone) to lose to qualify for 1-on-1 support call
rules.low_bmi_note: If lead has less than 29 BMI or <= 1 stone to lose, write 'One stone VETT later' in notes
rules.disqualification_criteria: Average salary < £35,000 GBP/year, active financial stress, Single Mum, or low finance red flags -> send Vett / Scholarship Vett instead of booking call directly

stages.name: Stage 0: Initial Weight & Height / Qualification
stages.description: Establish target weight loss and gather height/weight to calculate BMI and tailor the approach.
scripts: Alright [FirstName], Just so I know what to send you first, how much weight do you need to lose ideally?
[FirstName], how much weight do you need to lose ideally?
Alright [FirstName], just for clarity could you tell me your current body weight and height? As this completely changes what I need to send you first.
stages.notes: Ask current body weight and height only when they have less than or equal to 1 stone to lose. Write 'One stone VETT later' in notes if lead has less than 29 BMI.

stages.name: Stage 1: Question 1 - Core Barriers
stages.description: Diagnose the initial primary reason why losing weight and keeping it off has been difficult.
scripts: Alright [FirstName], What would you say is making it difficult for you to lose 2 stone & keep it off sustainably? Night time cravings? Stress or boredom eating? Injuries? Work related stress & lack of time? menopause? procrastination? You not coming first? Self Sabotage? Low motivation?
followups: [FirstName], what do you feel is making it difficult for you to lose this weight and keep it off sustainably?
Hey [FirstName], are the messages above coming through?

stages.name: Stage 2: Question 2 - Obstacle Deep Dives
stages.description: Specific empathetic diagnostic response based directly on what obstacle they answered in Question 1.

Injuries.script: [FirstName]. You mentioned injuries. If you could elaborate on this a little for me, please. Is this making stairs or hills difficult? Or where do you notice this the most?

Menopause.script: I hear you [FirstName], Menopause is a common struggle among women due to hormonal changes, poor sleep and a reduced metabolic rate! In addition to that, this affects our energy levels, which results in lower motivation to make changes in our day-to-day life... Does that make sense to you? Do you feel menopause is affecting your sleep, energy levels or food choices in any way?
Menopause.fup: [FirstName], is menopause affecting your eating habits, sleep, or energy levels in any way?
Menopause.note: 4 stages of Menopause: Premenopause, Perimenopause, Menopause, Post menopause. (Use Age message for pre/post menopause; replace menopause with perimenopause for perimenopausal women)

Lack of Willpower.script:
Surprisingly, willpower is not something that I want you to focus on just now; the perceived requirement of willpower tells me that what you have tried in the past has been a chore or requires discipline, which is usually not sustainable. You can’t hate it or feel deprived during it. Otherwise, it will never be sustainable. We have to also look for ways of making this easier and enjoyable. If it's not enjoyable, you won't sustain it.

On that note [FirstName], For clarity on your nutrition, could you tell me a bit more about your current food choices? What do your usual meals look like?

Eating Habits / Daily Meals.script:
I hear you [FirstName]... To get a better understanding of what's going on, could you provide some insights about your eating habits? Or what do your daily meals look like?

Also, how are your energy levels in the afternoon or evening? Do you ever feel sluggish in the morning?
Eating Habits / Daily Meals.fup: [FirstName], What do your current food choices look like?

Lack of Motivation.script: I hear you [FirstName]. Firstly, lack of motivation is something that we definitely need to address. It's a form of self-sabotage.... If I ask you honestly, is this lack of motivation due to past failed attempts, low energy, downplaying the problem, over confidence or fear of failure? What is behind the low motivation?

Comfort / Boredom Eating.script:
I hear you [FirstName], boredom eating is definitely a slippery slope and after we do it, we beat ourselves up and sometimes even speak to ourselves unkindly. To get a better understanding of what's going on, could you provide some insights about your eating habits? Or what do your daily meals look like?

Also, how are your energy levels throughout the day?

All of the Above.script: [FirstName], I'm impressed by your self-awareness that you can see all of the above are having an impact on you. However, if you had to pinpoint, then which of the above factors do you think you resonated with the most?
All of the Above.fup: [FirstName], Which of the above resonated with you the most?

Lack of Time.script:
I hear you [FirstName], and I completely get that – finding time is a real challenge when you're juggling multiple responsibilities. We all face this struggle but it is most certainly harder for women who get judged for not having a tidy house or for not having everything together, whereas there's rarely judgment if it's a man.

In Addition to that, People regain weight by saying 'I have to be in the right frame of mind' or 'I don’t have enough time' when facing challenges like work, family, or holidays.

What I've learned from experience is that investing a little time upfront to learn more efficient approaches actually saves time in the long run. It's like sharpening an axe before cutting wood – the initial effort pays off ten fold.

Many people also overestimate the time commitment needed. Just 20 minutes 3 times a week can make a meaningful difference IF we are doing the RIGHT things. And here's what I always remind myself: if we don't make time for our health now, we will eventually be forced to make time for illness. And this is true for everybody. I've spoken to ladies size 12 with weight-related strokes.

Can you resonate with any of that? :)
Lack of Time.fup: [FirstName], is lack of time due to your current working role? Or do you have other responsibilities?

Stress.script: I hear you [FirstName], Stress is one of the major weight loss inhibiting factors due to the changes in cortisol levels, is your stress due to your current working role? I mean is it quite stressful and challenging on a regular basis? Or do you have other responsibilities?
Stress.fup: [FirstName], is your stress level high due to your current working role?

Post Menopausal.script:
I hear you [FirstName], Weight loss definitely becomes harder or more complex with age as the hormonal changes can indeed add another layer of complexity... For clarity on your daily nutrition, could you tell me a bit more about your current food choices?? What do your daily meals look like?

Also, how are your energy levels in the late afternoon or evening? Do you ever find it hard to get up in the morning?

Underactive Thyroid.script: I hear you [FirstName], An Underactive thyroid can certainly makes things harder, but it's important that we don't believe that it will stop us from succeeding. It's very important that you know that now… Do you feel this is affecting your metabolic rate, eating habits, or energy levels in any way?
Underactive Thyroid.fup: [FirstName], do you feel your metabolic rate along with energy levels is getting affected by underactive thyroid?

Osteoarthritis.script: I hear you [FirstName], Osteoarthritis tends to add another layer of complexity when it comes to weight loss due to inflammation and joint pain. What everyday things are now becoming more difficult as a result of it?

Fibromyalgia.script: I hear you [FirstName], and fibro can be horrendous to deal with every day, living a life in pain or with low energy.It also tends to add another layer of complexity when it comes to weight loss due to its effects on muscles and joints throughout the body... Do you feel it is affecting your energy, motivation or sleep patterns in any way?

Diabetes.script: I hear you [FirstName], and I know it must be really tough for you to deal with this everyday because diabetes tends to add another layer of complexity when it comes to weight loss due to its effects on insulin levels and metabolism... Do you feel it is affecting your energy levels or food choices in any way?

Sciatica.script: I hear you [FirstName], and I know it must be extremely painful for you to deal with sciatica everyday. Sciatica tends to add another layer of complexity when it comes to weight loss due to its effects on lower back or lower body via the nerves.. Do you feel it is causing any mobility issues or restricting your physical activity in any way?

Not in Right Frame of Mind.script:
Thanks for sharing that. When someone says, "I'm not in the right frame of mind," it's usually because they're either overloaded or they feel like they're being pulled from pillar to post with one responsibility after another.
I hope you don't mind me challenging you but i’m doing it from a place of care what I mean by this is that the nicest possible way, is that you'll never be in the right of my mind. We also never miraculously become motivated. Movement creates motivation and similarly it's weight loss and self-development that actually, ironically, moves you into the right frame of mind. Also if we don't learn how to progress through times of challenge, then we're not battle-tested. That means that when inevitably life does throw curveballs at us, we are immediately sidelined and we regain the weight anyway. The ONLY way to make weight loss sustainable is learning how to do it DURING challenges. Couple this with improving energy, stress and sleep management plus overwhelm-reduction hacks, and these strategies drastically improve your coping skills.

This makes you a force to be reckoned with regardless of your professional success.

By the way, does that makes sense? :)

Procrastination.script:
Procrastination only ever happens for one of three reasons:
1. We downplay the problem or trivialise it, this happens usually when we're overconfident or say, "I know what I need to do." Even though if we haven't got the results that we want, it's a clear indicator that there are blind spots and things that we're not seeing.
2. We don't put ourselves first.
3. Deep down, we're afraid we'll fail, even though ironically, by not trying, we fail by default.
Which of these three do you think it is?

Not Coming First.script:
I'm not gonna say it's easy to prioritize yourself, because it's not. Society molds women in a way that associates guilt with self-prioritization. Work and family come first. You're the fixer.

The truth is, if we don't see the wood from the trees, then it becomes harder and harder for us to have the energy, mobility, and health to continue to help the people in life who matter. It's about foresight. Foresight to see that self-prioritization enables you to be able for longer to continue to help and support family. Can you see that?

Self Sabotage.script:
Self-sabotage has a variety of forms:
- undoing the hard work of exercise by eating high-calorie food
- putting up resistance
- not trusting or being skeptical
- sometimes being overconfident
- taking the foot off the gas after we've lost a certain amount of weight
This will never be addressed by "eat less, move more." and then every time we regain the weight, we feel like a failure. Does that make sense at all?

stages.name: Stage 3: Previous Diets & Knowledge Gaps
stages.description: Examine past diets and transition into the Knowledge Gap regarding age, metabolic rate, and outdated methods.

scripts.main: That does tell me a few things right away, and there's also going to be blind spots and nutritional gaps, that you're not aware of. If there were no nutritional gaps, then you'd already have the results that you want. What plans or diets have you tried in the past that didn't work for you longterm? And were these personalised?
followups: [FirstName], have you tried anything in the past to lose this weight??
[FirstName], what plans or diets have you tried in the past that didn’t work for you long-term?
scripts.optional_shallow_reply: Alright, how was your experience with them? Anything that didn't work out when you tried them? Also, your thoughts about their sustainability?
scripts.age_knowledge_gap:
[FirstName], When people usually come to me, it's because they've come to the realization that as we get older it gets harder, so "eating less and moving more" doesn't cut it anymore, there's usually more at play such as metabolic changes due to hormones, menopause, self-limiting beliefs or adherence to outdated methods…OR blind spots like I mentioned earlier!

That being said, I also need to know, what age were you when your weight was first on your radar for the very first time? and what age are you now?
scripts.unsustainable_diets_gap:
I am with you [FirstName], The truth is, popular diets that aren't tailored to you aren't sustainable and more often than not they're actually more damaging for your health than anything else. Many of them can lead to high blood pressure and an increased risk of heart disease. These diets can also leave you feeling like a failure. It's all because these methods weren't sustainable, That means it wasn't your fault. It was that the methodology was never sustainable. It is important that you see that to stop you from beating yourself up anymore.

That being said, I also need to know, what age were you when your weight was first on your radar for the very first time? and what age are you now?
scripts.combined_menopause_diets_gap:
I’m with you on this [FirstName], The truth is, popular diets that aren't tailored to you aren't sustainable and more often than not, they're actually more damaging for your health than anything else. When people usually come to me, it's because they've come to the realization that as we get older it gets harder, so "eating less and moving more" doesn't cut it anymore, there's usually more at play such as metabolic changes due to hormones, menopause, self-limiting beliefs or adherence to outdated methods…OR blind spots like I mentioned earlier!

That being said, I also need to know, what age were you when your weight was first on your radar for the very first time? and what age are you now?
scripts.fup_duration: [FirstName], basically what I’m trying to ask is, how long have you been struggling with this weight??
scripts.no_exact_number: I hear you, [FirstName]. Just to get a deeper sense of what's going on, how long has it really been, since your weight has been going up and down? How many years in total have you been trying to lose this weight?

stages.name: Stage 4: WHY NOW (Urgency & Driving Reasons)
stages.description: Establish why solving this now is critical before health degrades further.

scripts.normal:
A great way of looking at this is: if the fan belt in our car starts to make noise, we don't wait X number of years before we address it. We bring it to the garage before things become worse. When it comes to our weight, it's so easy to put things off or become overconfident because life or work gets in the way and family keeps coming first. While this might be difficult to look at, it's one of the strongest ways to prevent you from losing any more time.

One powerful way to create change is acknowledging what would happen if this was to keep getting worse. So if i ask you honestly where do you think you’d be in 5 years time if this was to keep getting worse? What are your 3 reasons as to why you want to make this a priority? WHY NOW?
scripts.with_years:
{Years} Years?? That’s over {Weeks} weeks [FirstName]... And if it's been going on that long, the time for thinking about it is long gone as this is already taken up far too much headspace!

Another real challenge is that weight gain happens slowly. We don’t expect the weight to go up but because it gets consistently harder as we get older it inevitably does keep going up despite our best efforts. What worked in the past stops working.

One powerful way to create change is acknowledging what would happen if this was to keep getting worse. So if i ask you honestly where do you think you’d be in 5 years time if this was to keep getting worse? What are your 3 reasons as to why you want to make this a priority? WHY NOW?
scripts.oversharers: {Years} years, That’s quite a long struggle [FirstName], this obviously will have taken up a lot of headspace as well… I feel as if you’ve touched on this already, but if I ask you honestly, what are your 3 WHYs to lose this weight now & keep it off sustainably for the rest of your life? Three reasons that motivate you to make this change now before it becomes even harder for you to fix?
scripts.december_exclusive:
{Years} years, that's over {Weeks} weeks. [FirstName], I also want to commend you on the fact that you've been proactive with this. So many people put this off until the 'new year, new me' facade kicks in. And ultimately, this leads to us never being battle-tested, because learning how to progress in times of challenge is actually essential if we want this to be sustainable.

Christmas comes around every year, and the last thing you want is to be starting in January a stone heavier. So, well done on being proactive and not falling for the 'new year, new me' facade!

Now, if I ask you honestly, what are your reasons for not putting this off or falling for the 'new year, new me' facade? Why is addressing this now a priority to you? WHY NOW?
followups: [FirstName], What would be your top 3 WHYs to lose this weight and keep it off sustainably for the rest of your life?

The truth is, if we don't understand our WHYs, or why changing something is genuinely important to us, it means we kind of just go about our day-to-day and just put the thoughts about our weight on a back burner. So, tell me, What are your 3 WHYs to lose this weight now??

stages.name: Stage 5: Pain Generation & Medical History
stages.description: Deepen the emotional pain/safeguarding motivation and check family medical history.

scripts.pain_generating: Addressing this is obviously important to you, especially considering your {POINTS_FROM_3_WHYS}! Just to get a deeper sense of what's going on... In what scenarios do you feel self-conscious about your weight? Also our health is often more fragile than we think. I don't want to do a health scare before we prioritize this. What health conditions in particular are you looking to avoid?, or is it that you want to be proactive in safeguarding your health, or is it both?
pain_followups: [FirstName], When does your weight or health bother you the most in your day-to-day life?
Hey [FirstName], did My last message coming through?
scripts.medical_history: Lastly, just before I give you some advice, do you have any health conditions that I should be aware of? Or is there any history of heart disease, stroke, cancer or diabetes in the family?
medical_followups: Hey [FirstName], do you have any health issues that I’m not aware of?
scripts.frequency_question:
I am with you [FirstName], Lastly just before I give you some advice, how often do you think about this, is it like once a week, once a month? How often do you think about your weight?

Lastly, just before I give you some advice, do you have any health conditions that I should be aware of? Or is there any history of heart disease, stroke, cancer or diabetes in the family?

stages.name: Stage 6: The 1-on-1 Call Pitch
stages.description: Transition the lead onto a complimentary 45-60 min support call to uncover blind spots.

scripts.normal:
Alright [FirstName], Considering what you’ve shared with me so far, this Definitely needs to be addressed on a 1‑on‑1 Weight Loss Support Session because the last thing you want now is to be in the exact same place in 3 months time... Especially when if we don’t make time for our health, we will eventually have to make time for illness later.

We do this call over the phone (and it is complimentary by the way) to show you your current blindspots in your nutrition, training and behavioural patterns. There are ALWAYS blind spots btw, and showing them to you is the easiest way for you to lose the first stone sustainably.

I've just moved a few things around to open up a few slots because of the extent of what you've already told me …….. The call is about 45-60 minutes and requires you to have a pen/paper to take notes in a quiet place because I want you to get the most out of it. Which time could you make work?

P.S. You will not be sold anything on this call. This is purely about learning more about your current situation and giving you clarity on what needs to change.
I've got availability between 1:15 pm-6 pm today or tomorrow between 10 am-7 pm. The call is about 10-15 minutes and requires you to have a pen/paper to take notes in a quiet place because I want you to get the most out of it. Which time could you make work?
scripts.scholarship:
Congratulations [FirstName], you've made it to the next round of our Scholarships! The next step is to set up a One-to-one weight loss session. We do this call over the phone (and it is complimentary btw) for us to learn why sustainable weight loss is genuinely a priority to you.
We will also identify current gaps or blind spots in your nutrition, training, or your behavioural patterns. Finding a gap is actually a good thing btw, it means we can make a couple of quick and easy changes to help you lose the first 3-6kg relatively easily without overwhelming you.
scripts.medical_history:
Alright [FirstName], so we do have direct family history, the reason why I did ask about family history there, is because this is what most people don't realize... losing weight isn't only about the effort, it's also about how your body is wired. So two people can do the exact same thing - eat the same food, do the same exercises and yet one of them drops weight easily, while the other person doesn't progress, which is really frustrating.

From what you’ve shared with me so far, this definitely needs to be addressed on a 1‑on‑1 Weight Loss Support Session because the last thing you want now is to be in the exact same place in 3 months time (When we don’t make time for our health, we will have to make time for Illness later)

I've just opened up a few slots for you …….. The call is about 45-60 minutes and requires you to have a pen/paper to take notes in a quiet place because I want you to get the most out of it. Which of these times could you make work?
scripts.check_confirm_later: P.S. Our slots for support calls are in quite high demand, especially when they are free just now, so it's possible that times will be changed later and your desired spot will be taken by someone else... So let me know as soon as you can :)
scripts.times_offered_no_booking:
[FirstName], The most important part of this one-to-one session, by the way, is to teach you easy-to-implement strategies on how to reset your metabolism. This will be one of the many reasons why what you're currently doing isn't getting you the results that you want. Let me have a look again and see what times we still have available. Especially considering you've just told me this has been going on for {Years} years OR especially you just told me that there is a direct family medical history. Hang on a sec.

(Pause for 2 mins)

Okay, so I spoken to the team and we've opened up {TIMES}. Which of these can you make work? And I'll see if I can hold that for you.
scripts.rescheduling: No worries [FirstName], I’ll move a few things around for you, because I know this has been going on for {Years} years and I know it's important to you... I've just opened up a few slots for you (ADD TIMES)... Which time works best for you?

objections.negative_review_or_trustpilot:
Hello,
I understand how seeing a negative review could give you pause. We’re all naturally wired to notice the negative comments over the many positive ones.

What I would gently suggest, though, is not to take everything you read online at face value. In our experience, the very small percentage of negative reviews — around 2% — have come from situations where we’ve shown significant flexibility, extended payment plans, additional support, and a great deal of goodwill, and sadly in a few cases that goodwill has unfortunately been taken advantage of.

That said, the bigger picture matters. We have a 98% success rate and 98% of our reviews are overwhelmingly positive. Those reflect the real experience of the vast majority of people we serve. And realistically, 98% of people can’t all be wrong. We stand by our work and our results.

Rather than being influenced by the minority, perhaps the fairest thing to do is to speak with us directly over the phone so you can experience how we operate for yourself. That way, you can make up your own mind based on your own judgement rather than relying solely on what you’ve read online.

Does that sound fair? And please let me know if you feel I’m being unreasonable. I’m always open to hearing your perspective.
objections.prefer_email:
Hey [FirstName], I totally get where you're coming from and I actually like emailing myself. The challenge, though, is that things can be interpreted differently over text and can be addressed so much more effectively via a call. Especially when we have so many people reaching out to us, it obviously saves us time and also saves you time as well, particularly when our support calls are so detailed and tailored to the individual. There’s just so much that goes into it, like your history, lifestyle, habits, and goals—that it’s not really something we can fully cover over email or by texts in any way.

From the support call alone you will gain understanding as to WHERE you've been going wrong what’s been holding them back, uncovering blind spots, or figuring out why the weight keeps coming back.

Would you be open to giving the call a try? If so, which of the times I shared earlier could work for you? Also imagine how you're gonna feel in a couple of months' time when you've kept this commitment to yourself and you're well over a stone down.
